topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Cancer development as disruption of normal cellular differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how acquired cellular changes disrupt normal tissue organisation and why cancer must be studied in that tissue context.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign tumours from invasive and metastatic malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish spread beyond a tumour's original boundaries as a feature of malignancy and illustrate how that spread is recognised.

topics.label: Tumour progression and the significance of benign status
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what a tumour's benign or invasive status implies for its subsequent course, showing that benign growth neither inevitably becomes malignant nor guarantees harmlessness.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and produces potentially fatal disease.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumour types across human and animal populations.

topics.label: Cancer presentation and the effectiveness of screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the need for early detection and assess how effectively screening can identify treatable disease in different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture close and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students towards revision and upcoming teaching.
